quest.title: In Search of Lost Time: South
quest.description: Researcher Broglie wants to retrieve the sunken hydrology research data...
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x250, Primogem x30, Mora x30000, Hero's Wit x2

dialogues.speaker: Broglie
dialogues.text: Oh, what am I to do...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Are you okay? Sighing so sadly alone by the water like that... Did something bad happen?

dialogues.speaker: Broglie
dialogues.text: Yes, and it wasn't any old "something bad," but something awful...

dialogues.speaker: Broglie
dialogues.text: Ah! Apologies, I forgot to introduce myself. My name is Broglie, and I'm an entry-level researcher at the Fontaine Research Institute, and I was previously responsible for monitoring Fontaine's hydrology data.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh, what's "hydrology data"?

dialogues.speaker: Broglie
dialogues.text: *ahem* Simply put, it is all the data related to the various properties of water. For example, there's the temperature of various water layers, water level, rates of current flow and evaporation within set times, concentration of dissolved impurities...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, that all sounds really complicated!

dialogues.speaker: Broglie
dialogues.text: It is, that's why people are needed — specifically, my colleagues and I — to collect this complex data and make observations so that we can detect changes in the water quality in advance.

dialogues.speaker: Broglie
dialogues.text: If no one does this work, by the time we discover a huge problem, it will be too late to address it.

dialogues.speaker: Broglie
dialogues.text: You know, that's one of the reasons those lovely Oceanids left Fontaine. There was a change in the water quality that made it unsuitable for them to live in—

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Well... That's what I was told during my induction training, probably to rouse a semblance of personal responsibility in us. The point is, monitoring the hydrology data is pretty important work!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: For instance, if a change in water quality nears the minimum coefficient, it could make the taste less smooth and refreshing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? That's all?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Haha, well, that's what makes it the minimum coefficient, right? But if things got out of hand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What, would the water turn into Fonta?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: No, it would probably just lead to a mass extinction event all over Fontaine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a minute, does that mean you're sighing here by yourself because something terrible has happened to the water...?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Oh, not at all. It's just that the monitoring data I gathered have sunk to the bottom along with the observation station, and I don't know how I can fish them back out. That's what's got me so worried.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... the observation station, too?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Yes. I imagine you've heard about that awful lab accident from before. You know, the one that blew the Central Laboratory sky high.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: As ill-luck would have it, that lab accident also sunk the hydrology observation station here. Fortunately, my colleagues and I were doing a study somewhere else at the time, so we weren't hurt.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: But the years of hydrology monitoring data we've collated are all still down there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that does sound quite serious...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll take care of it.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: #Really!? Aaaah! Kind {M#sir}{F#lady}, if you can help me, I'll be in your debt for the rest of my life!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: You should know that, ever since the observation station sank, the former departments had to be reorganized, and I was transferred to the newly established Department of Hydrology and Aquatic Life Conservation!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Not only is the department head breathing down my neck all day, but there are all these new, inexplicable rules...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: We have to report for duty on time, and we still have to make this weekly report at the end of each week! We can't even openly take our afternoon naps in the office anymore!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Even worse, there's a woman who keeps a Blubberbeast in the office. A Blubberbeast! It's bitten me three times already!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: So, if our research data from before can be retrieved, I'll be able to think of a way to persuade my supervisor to restore the Hydrology Monitoring Department...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: That way, my colleagues and I can also be transferred back to our original posts and return to happy lives of ease...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Ahem. I mean, return to fulfilling lives of field studies!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So after all that, you just want to slack off, don't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Why don't you just go down there and get that stuff yourself?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Well, this is embarrassing, but even though the Fontaine Research Institute did organize diving training sessions, we strategically held a dinner each time...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Uh, I mean, every diving training session conflicted with our dinner reservation at Hotel Debord. What a shame!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: #A—Anyway, the advancement of the science of hydrology and the future of Fontaine are in your hands, kind {M#sir}{F#lady}!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: As for your reward, worry not — as long as you can help me recover my research, I'll do everything in my power to ensure you're adequately compensated!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: So, I'm begging you, please retrieve our precious data from the central control room for me！

talks.objective: Enter the sunken hydrology research station

dialogues.speaker: Broglie
dialogues.text: #I'm counting on you to retrieve that data, kind {M#sir}{F#lady}!

dialogues.speaker: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
dialogues.text: (This notebook must have been made of a water-resistant material — it's still in perfect condition even after all this time. There's also a sticky note on the cover.)

dialogues.speaker: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
dialogues.text: "This is already the third time! Remember to follow the instructions precisely when operating! If we lose the data again, we won't get any more afternoon snacks for the month!"

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Flip through the notebook.)

dialogues.speaker: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
dialogues.text: "...Standard Data Export Procedure: Confirm the energy storage device below the main console is online (in accordance with the Fontaine Research Institute Energy Conservation Regulation D-503, the device is turned off by default)..."

dialogues.speaker: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
dialogues.text: "...When energy supply is normal, the green indicator on the main console will light up. At this time, pull the control lever on the left marked "DO NOT TOUCH OR ELSE" to print out the observation data..."

dialogues.speaker: Conch Madeleine Stop Safe Operating Procedures
dialogues.text: "...Data should be printed at least once every 3 months, or else some data may be lost..."

talks.objective: Find a way to charge the research terminal

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is this what you wanted?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Aaah... Yes, this is it, this is it! But... you haven't even gone into the water yet, how do you already have the data?

choices.text: We've been to the place before.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: I see... Thank you! That's all the data from this station now recovered!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's good... Wait a minute, did you say "this station"?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Yes! We have three observation stations and one central processing station in total, each with their own independent datasets.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: So, in order to convey the need for monitoring to my supervisor, the data from the remaining two stations still needs to be recovered and then analyzed at the central processing station...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, alright, Paimon will bite — do you also need us to salvage the other two stations?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Oh, of course not! The other two observation stations were spared from the lab disaster and continue to stand proudly on solid ground!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a relief...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: It's just that... those two stations have been taken over by some fellows from Snezhnaya...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From Snezhnaya... Hang on, you're not talking about the Fatui, are you?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: That's them! They claimed that they got permission from the Maison Gestion to take over the stations. They won't let us anywhere near them, let alone retrieve the data.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: As for the Maison Gestion... As you may know, verifying anything with the Maison Gestion is harder than trying to catch lightning in a bottle.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds a little suspicious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, since it's the Fatui we're talking about, they might actually be planning to use the observation stations to do something bad...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon doesn't super want to help, but... *sigh* {NICKNAME}, we should take a look just in case...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: #Thank you so much, kind {M#sir}{F#lady}! I'll mark the locations of the Pate de Fruit Station and Crepes Suzette Station on your map now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aren't these all food names?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Yes! And they do sound sweet and tasty, don't they? Just the way life ought to be!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: By the way, this place is the Conch Madeleine Station. Imagine, if you would, breaking off a small piece of Conch Madeleine, steeping it in warm water or Tisane, and drinking it all up...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: That's what our tea times were like before. *sigh* I never thought the station would end up sinking like this...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Anyway, for me to be happy and free again... I mean, for scientific advancement and the future of humanity, I'm counting on you to help me recover that old monitoring data!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, it wasn't magic! We just happened to go there by chance previously!

talks.objective: Use the research terminal to access the hydrology research data

dialogues.speaker: Paimon

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What does the instruction manual say... Okay, next, we just need to pull that lever that says "Do NOT touch under any circumstances!" on it, and we can export the recorded data...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: For instance, if a change in water quality nears the minimum coefficient, it could make the taste less smooth and refreshing...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What? That's all?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Haha, well, that what makes it the minimum coefficient, right? But if things got out of hand...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: What, will the water turn into Fonta?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: No, it would probably just lead to a mass extinction event all over Fontaine.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wait a minute, does that mean you're sighing here by yourself because something terrible has happened to the water...?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Oh, not at all. It's just that the monitoring data I gathered have sunk to the bottom along with the observation station, and I don't know how I can fish them back out. That's what's got me so worried.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Um... the observation station, too?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Yes. I imagine you've heard about that awful lab accident from before. You know, the one that blew the Central Laboratory sky high.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: As ill-luck would have it, that lab accident also sunk the hydrology observation station here. Fortunately, my colleagues and I were doing a study somewhere else at the time, so we weren't hurt.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: But the years of hydrology monitoring data we've collated are all still down there...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that does sound quite serious...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We'll take care of it.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: #Really!? Aaaah! Kind {M#sir}{F#lady}, if you can help me, I'll be in your debt for the rest of my life!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: You should know that, ever since the observation station sank, the former departments had to be reorganized, and I was transferred to the newly established Department of Hydrology and Aquatic Life Conservation!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Not only is the department head breathing down my neck all day, but there are all these new, inexplicable rules...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: We have to report for duty on time, and we still have to make this weekly report at the end of each week! We can't even openly take our afternoon naps in the office anymore!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Even worse, there's a woman who keeps a Blubberbeast in the office. A Blubberbeast! It's bitten me three times already!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: So, if our research data from before can be retrieved, I'll be able to think of a way to persuade my supervisor to restore the Hydrology Monitoring Department...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: That way, my colleagues and I can also be transferred back to our original posts and return to happy lives of ease...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Ahem. I mean, return to fulfilling lives of field studies!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: So after all that, you just want to slack off, don't you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah! Why don't you just go down there and get that stuff yourself?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Well, this is embarrassing, but even though the Fontaine Research Institute did organize diving training sessions, we strategically held a dinner each time...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Uh, I mean, every diving training session conflicted with the dinner reservations we'd already made at Hotel Debord. What a shame!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: #A—Anyway, the advancement of the science of hydrology and the future of Fontaine are in your hands, kind {M#sir}{F#lady}!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: As for your reward, worry not — As long as you can help me recover my research, I'll do everything in my power to ensure you're adequately compensated!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: So, I'm begging you, please help me retrieve our precious data from the central control room!

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Is this what you wanted?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Aaah... Yes, this is it, this is it! But... you haven't even gone into the water yet, how do you already have the data?

choices.text: We've been to the place before.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: I see... Thank you! That's all the data from this station now recovered!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Well, that's good... Wait a minute, did you say "this station"?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Yes! We have three observation stations and one central processing station in total, each with their own independent datasets.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: So, in order to convey the need for monitoring to my supervisor, the data from the remaining two stations still needs to be recovered and then analyzed at the central processing station...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh, alright, Paimon will bite — do you also need us to salvage the other two stations?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Oh, of course not! The other two observation stations were spared from the lab disaster and continue to stand proudly on solid ground!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's a relief...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: It's just that... those two stations have been taken over by some fellows from Snezhnaya...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: From Snezhnaya... Hang on, you're not talking about the Fatui, are you?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: That's them! They claimed that they got permission from the Maison Gestion to take over the stations. They won't let us anywhere near them, let alone retrieve the data.

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: As for the Maison Gestion... As you may know, verifying anything with the Maison Gestion is harder than trying to catch lightning in a bottle.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Sounds a little suspicious.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Yeah, since it's the Fatui we're talking about, they might actually be planning to use the observation stations to do something bad...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Paimon doesn't super want to help, but... *sigh* {NICKNAME}, we should take a look just in case...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: #Thank you so much, kind {M#sir}{F#lady}! I'll mark the locations of the Pate de Fruit Station and Crepes Suzette Station on your map now!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Aren't these all food names?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Yes! And they do sound sweet and tasty, don't they? Just the way life ought to be!

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: By the way, this place is the Conch Madeleine Station. Imagine, if you would, breaking off a small piece of Conch Madeleine, steeping it in warm water or Tisane, and drinking it all up...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: That's what our tea times were like before. *sigh* I never thought the station would end up sinking like this...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Anyway, for me to be happy and free again... I mean, for scientific advancement and the future of humanity, I'm counting on you to help me recover that old monitoring data!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? Wait a minute, now that Paimon's looking at these locations, it seems like we've already been to them before...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Huh!? Really?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We've already sent those Fatui running for the hills.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: And, we already have that data you're looking for...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You show Broglie the paper tapes you got earlier...

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: Ahhhh! Yes, this is it, this is it! You two are angels, angels sent from the heavens to save me from my misery and return me to my happy life of ease—

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hey! What about all that science stuff?

response.speaker: Broglie
response.text: #Anyway, there's no time to lose, kind {M#sir}{F#lady}! Please come with me to the Fontaine Research Institute to find my supervisor and request the key to the central processing station!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Come on, it wasn't magic! We just happened to go there by chance previously!
